subject: sociology
title: Stratification & Differentiation: Gender & Feminism Waves
welcome_lead: Three waves and counting — how feminism evolved.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology stratification gender feminism waves liberal radical Marxist.
final_note: Patriarchy is contested, reformed, and theorised differently in each wave.

walkthroughs.body_html: First wave (late 1800s-1920s): suffrage; UK Representation of People Act 1918 gave women over 30 the vote, 1928 equalised it. Second wave (1960s-80s): Equal Pay 1970, Sex Discrimination 1975. Third wave (1990s+): intersectionality, body politics, queer critique.

Liberal feminism: equality through reform (Friedan 1963). Marxist feminism: patriarchy serves capitalism (Benston 1969 — women's domestic labour subsidises capital). Radical feminism: patriarchy is the primary oppression (Firestone 1970 — biology is the foundation).

Crenshaw (1989): black women experience compound oppression of race + gender — neither feminism nor anti-racism alone captures it. bell hooks critiques white middle-class second-wave feminism. Walby (1990): six structures of patriarchy — household, work, state, violence, sexuality, culture.
